filename: Informing Depositional Ice Growth Models Through 3-D Reconstruction of Ice Crystal Images Using Machine Learning.pdf
title: Informing Depositional Ice Growth Models Through 3-D Reconstruction of Ice Crystal Images Using Machine Learning
venue: 2024 CESM Atmosphere Model Working Group (AMWG) Meeting
parameterization_target: ice crystal depositional growth and mass/area-dimensional relationships
code_availability: Developed in Python, code + dataset will be open-source and reproducible
testbed_rationale: The synthetic training dataset and code are noted as planned to be open-source, but no URL or repository is provided in the presentation slides.
pain_points: Observational probes (e.g., CPI) yield only 2D projection images, causing ambiguity in true 3D crystal mass, surface area, and arm count
Classification of arm count from 2D projection features showed lower skill and confusion between adjacent classes
Need to scale habit models from single-crystal synthetic rosettes to broader real-world ice particle habit mixtures
extraction_notes: Document consists of presentation slides given at the CESM AMWG meeting on February 14, 2024. The slides describe ML prediction of 3D crystal geometric attributes (effective density, effective surface area, number of arms) from 2D projections to constrain mass-dimension (m-D) and area-dimension (A-D) relations in depositional ice growth models (e.g., P3, PUMAS).
